questions.q: Which converter type changes DC into AC?
questions.explain: An inverter converts DC to AC; a rectifier does AC to DC and a chopper DC to DC.

questions.q: Why can power converters reach high efficiency?
options: Their devices work as switches, fully on or fully off
questions.explain: An on switch has almost no voltage and an off switch almost no current, so little power is lost in it.

questions.q: What is the average output voltage of a half-wave diode rectifier with a resistive load?
In a half-wave rectifier with an RL load, why does the output go negative for part of the cycle?
options: The inductor keeps the diode conducting after π until the current reaches zero
The supply has a DC offset
questions.explain: Stored inductor energy keeps the current flowing to the extinction angle β > π.

questions.q: A three-phase diode bridge is fed from a supply with a peak phase voltage of 200 V. What is the average output voltage?
For how long does each diode in a three-phase bridge conduct per cycle?
questions.explain: Each diode conducts for 120°, in two 60° line-voltage segments.

questions.q: What is the peak inverse voltage of each diode in a three-phase bridge ($V_m$ = peak phase voltage)?
questions.explain: A diode blocks the peak line-to-line voltage, $\sqrt3V_m$.

questions.q: A half-wave controlled rectifier with a resistive load has $V_m = 339.4$ V and α = 40°. What is the average output voltage?
A full-wave controlled rectifier with a resistive load has $V_m = 339.4$ V and α = 40°. What is the average output voltage?
A single-phase full converter with continuous current is fed at 240 V rms with α = 40°. What is the average output voltage?
A single-phase full converter with a highly inductive load is fired at α = 120°. What happens?
options: It rectifies with a positive average voltage
The average output voltage is negative, so with a source in the load it inverts
questions.explain: $V_{av} = \frac{2V_m}{\pi}\cos\alpha < 0$ for α > 90°: inverter operation when the load has an EMF.

questions.q: With continuous current, what is the rms output voltage of a single-phase full converter fed at V rms?
questions.explain: The output follows the supply for a full half cycle (α to π + α), so $V_{rms} = V$.

questions.q: If FF is the form factor, what is the ripple factor?
What is the voltage ripple factor of a single-phase full converter with continuous current at α = 0?
As α approaches 90° in a full converter with continuous current, the voltage ripple factor…
questions.explain: The mean output $0.9V\cos\alpha$ tends to zero while the AC part does not, so $RF_v \to \infty$. The slides' "maximum 1.11" is wrong.

questions.q: Which harmonics appear in the output voltage of a single-phase full converter?
questions.explain: The output repeats every half cycle of the supply, so only even harmonics of the supply frequency appear.

questions.q: A full converter feeds R = 10 Ω, L = 50 mH at 50 Hz (φ = 57.5°). At α = 75°, the current is…
questions.explain: With no back EMF, conduction is continuous only while α < φ = tan⁻¹(ωL/R).

questions.q: What is the natural power-factor angle φ (in degrees) of R = 10 Ω, L = 50 mH at 50 Hz?
A full converter at 240 V, α = 45°, continuous current, feeds 10 Ω in series with 50 mH and a 50 V EMF. What is the average load current?
A three-phase fully controlled bridge on a 415 V (line) supply runs with continuous current at α = 30°. What is the average output voltage?
In a three-phase fully controlled bridge, how often is a thyristor fired?
questions.explain: Six thyristors are fired in sequence every 60°, giving six pulses per cycle.

questions.q: A three-phase full converter carries a ripple-free 120 A DC current. What is the rms line current?
What is the supply power factor of a three-phase full converter with ripple-free current at α = 60°?
For a resistive load, when does a three-phase full converter's output current become discontinuous?
questions.explain: Above 60° the line voltage reaches zero within a conduction interval; then $V_o = 2.34V[1 + \cos(\alpha + 60°)]$.

questions.q: A buck converter steps 48 V down to 12 V in continuous conduction. What is the duty cycle?
Find the minimum inductance (in µH) for continuous current in a buck converter with δ = 0.4, R = 6 Ω and f = 5 kHz.
In a buck converter in discontinuous conduction, the output voltage…
options: depends on the load as well as δ
questions.explain: In DCM $V_c/E = K[-1 + \sqrt{1 + 2/K}]$ with $K = TR\delta^2/4L$, which contains R.

questions.q: A buck converter has D = 0.75, L = 0.75 mH, C = 0.47 µF and f = 50 kHz. What is the output ripple $\Delta V_o/V_o$ in percent?
A boost converter raises 40 V to 150 V. What is δ?
A boost converter supplies 6 A to its load at δ = 0.733. What is the average inductor current?
In a boost converter, what feeds the load while the switch is on?
questions.explain: The diode is reverse biased while the switch is on, so the capacitor supplies the load; hence $\Delta V_o = I_o\delta/(fC)$.

questions.q: A buck-boost converter must give 50 V from 35 V. What duty cycle is needed?
A buck-boost converter runs at δ = 0.4. Its output is…
options: higher than the input, same polarity

questions.q: What is the main advantage of the Ćuk converter over the buck-boost converter?
questions.explain: Inductors in series with both input and output make both currents continuous; energy is transferred by $C_1$.

questions.q: A Ćuk converter has E = 12 V and δ = 0.6. What is the magnitude of the output voltage?
Which DC–DC converter can operate in all four quadrants?
questions.explain: The full-bridge converter has bidirectional voltage and current, so it can also act as an inverter.

questions.q: A half-bridge inverter has V = 48 V. What is the rms fundamental output voltage?
A full-bridge square-wave inverter has $V_d = 220$ V. What is the rms fundamental output voltage?
Why are feedback diodes connected across the switches of an inverter?
options: To carry the load current after a switch turns off with an inductive load, returning energy to the supply
questions.explain: With an RL load the current cannot reverse instantly; it flows through the diodes back to the DC source.

questions.q: A six-step inverter runs from $V_d = 600$ V. What is the rms line-to-line output voltage?
Which harmonics are absent from the line voltage of a six-step inverter?
questions.explain: The pole voltages are odd-symmetric (no even harmonics), and their triplen harmonics are in phase, so they cancel in $v_{AB} = v_{AO} - v_{BO}$.

questions.q: In a six-step inverter with a star resistive load, during an interval with S1, S5 and S6 on, the phase voltage $v_{BN}$ is…
questions.explain: A and C are on the positive rail, B on the negative: $v_{BN} = -\frac{2V_d}{3R}R = -\frac23V_d$.

questions.q: A multiple-pulse PWM inverter has a 1 kHz carrier and a 50 Hz output. How many pulses per half cycle?
A single-pulse PWM full bridge has $V_d = 220$ V and a pulse width of 90°. What is the rms output voltage?
What is the modulation index in PWM?
questions.explain: $M = A_r/A_c$, the reference amplitude over the carrier amplitude.

questions.q: In unipolar SPWM, how are the two legs of a full bridge controlled?
options: Both from the same comparison, switching together
Leg A from $A_r$ vs $A_c$ and leg B from $-A_r$ vs $A_c$
questions.explain: The legs switch independently, so the output steps between $\pm V_d$ and 0.
